name: InterStim FI pivotal study
question: Among patients with fecal incontinence who respond to test stimulation, how often does InterStim implantation reduce weekly incontinence episodes by at least half?

design.population: Adults with chronic fecal incontinence (>2 frank stool-loss episodes/week for >6 months, or >12 months after vaginal delivery) after conservative treatment failure or ineligibility; 120/133 test-stimulated candidates received chronic InterStim implantation. Excluded external anal sphincter defects over 60 degrees and uncontrolled watery diarrhea.
design.description: Prospective 16-center single-arm study (2002–2008); acute and 10–14-day subchronic test stimulation before implantation

verdictNote: The 12-month primary objective was met in 88/106 evaluable implanted patients.
takeaway: In a prospective single-arm study of 120 implanted test responders, 88/106 (83%) with 12-month diaries had at least 50% fewer weekly fecal incontinence episodes (95% CI 74%–90%; P < 0.0001), meeting the prespecified objective; a missing-data analysis estimated 73%.

reports.label: 12-month pivotal report
reports.dateLocator: Crossref and PubMed give March 2010 issue; exact online publication date not verified
reports.citation: Wexner SD, Coller JA, Devroede G, et al. "Sacral Nerve Stimulation for Fecal Incontinence: Results of a 120-Patient Prospective Multicenter Study." *Ann Surg.* 2010;251(3):441-449. doi:10.1097/SLA.0b013e3181cf8ed0
reports.followUp: Mean 28 months (range 2.2-69.5 months); primary endpoint at 12 months

results.measure: At least 50% reduction in weekly incontinent episodes at 12 months versus baseline
results.note: Complete-case analysis of implanted patients with evaluable 12-month bowel diaries; exact binomial test against a 50% null. Modified worst-case analysis counted missing outcomes as failure unless subsequent data were available.
Complete-case 12-month bowel-diary cohort; 41% shown in Figure 1.

results.measure: Mean episodes per week at baseline and 12 months
results.note: Within-group paired comparison; no comparator arm.

results.measure: At least 50% reduction in weekly incontinent episodes at 24 months
results.note: Complete-case 24-month bowel-diary cohort; follow-up beyond the 12-month primary endpoint.

results.measure: At least 50% reduction in weekly incontinent days at 12 months
results.note: Prespecified secondary objective tested against a 50% null in the complete-case cohort.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 442; Results, p 444, Table 1

results.measure: At least 50% reduction in weekly incontinent episodes at 12 months with modified worst-case imputation

values.snm: 88/120 (73%); 66% when 13 test failures/withdrawal included among 133 tested

results.note: Missing 12-month data counted as failure unless later data existed; the tested-cohort analysis also includes 13 not chronically implanted.
results.locator: Full text, Statistical Analysis, p 443; Results, p 444

harms.label: Unanticipated adverse device effects
harms.locator: Full text, Abstract, p 441; Adverse Events, p 445
harms.note: No unanticipated adverse device effects; anticipated device- or therapy-related adverse events occurred.

harms.label: Device- or therapy-related adverse events

values.snm: 307 events in 96/120 patients (80%); 26/307 serious events; implant-site pain 31/120 (25.8%), paresthesia 15/120 (12.5%)

harms.note: Cumulative at the primary-report cutoff; serious-event count is events, not patients.

harms.label: Implant-site infection and surgical treatment

values.snm: 13/120 (10.8%) infections; 7/120 (5.8%) required surgery: 5/120 (4.2%) explants and 2/120 (1.7%) replacements

harms.note: Primary-report adjudication; the 2011 report reclassified one infection onset to the test phase.

delivery.label: Test stimulation and implantation
delivery.value: Of 285 screened at 16 centers, 133 underwent acute test stimulation, 129 entered subchronic testing, and 120/133 (90.2%) received chronic implantation after test-phase improvement.

delivery.label: Lead placement and stimulation
delivery.value: Quadripolar lead at S3 in 112/120, S4 in 5/120 and S2 in 3/120; 112/120 received a tined lead. External stimulation lasted 10–14 days; the implanted generator was placed in a contralateral gluteal pocket; recommended programming variables were a 210-microsecond pulse width and 15 Hz.
delivery.locator: Full text, Study Procedures and Results, p 443
delivery.note: Permanent implantation followed ≥50% improvement in weekly incontinent episodes and/or days during testing.

reports.dateLocator: Crossref and PubMed give September 2011 issue; exact online publication date not verified

reports.followUp: Mean 3.1 years (range 0.2–6.1); 83 completed all or part of 3-year assessment, 77/120 had 3-year bowel diaries

results.note: Complete-case 3-year bowel-diary cohort; 83 completed all or part of the assessment.

results.measure: At least 50% reduction in weekly incontinent episodes at 3 years among 120 implanted patients

values.snm: 95/120 (79%) with last observation carried forward; 71/120 (59%) with modified worst-case imputation

results.note: Both sensitivity analyses used all 120 implanted patients; 43 lacked 3-year bowel diaries.
results.locator: Full text, Statistical Analysis, p 1067; Results, pp 1069, 1071

harms.label: Device- or therapy-related adverse events through mean 3.1-year follow-up

values.snm: Implant-site pain 28% of 120 implanted; paresthesia 15% of 120; altered stimulation sensation 12% of 120; implant-site infection 12/120 (10%)

harms.note: Cumulative after chronic implantation at the 2010-02-08 cutoff; the article gives percentages but not patient numerators for pain, paresthesia or altered sensation. One infection was reclassified as test-phase onset.

harms.label: Infection requiring surgery

harms.locator: Full text, Adverse Events and Discussion, pp 1071, 1073
harms.note: Twelve postimplant infection events; one superficial infection resolved spontaneously and five with medication.

delivery.label: Long-term retention
delivery.value: 76/120 implanted patients (63.3%) were followed at least 5 years; 74 completed a 5-year visit and 72 had evaluable episode diaries.

delivery.label: Test stimulation
delivery.value: A 10–14-day subchronic test stimulation preceded permanent implantation after at least 50% improvement in weekly incontinent episodes and/or days.
